Exposure multiplication occurs before luminance Reinhard mapping and neutral-axis gamut compression. For fixed positive adapted luminance/chromaticity, output channels are nondecreasing: before upper-bound compression they scale with monotone L=Y/(1+Y); after that bound activates they equal L+(1-L)*(r_i-1)/(r_max-1). sRGB encoding preserves this ordering. This is algebraic source review, not an executed numerical sweep.

Negative/nonfinite input XYZ and nonfinite or negative adapted luminance return nil; zero adapted luminance returns black. Finite valid settings keep adaptation/exposure bounded. Production paths accumulate nonnegative bounded blackbody light contributions rather than arbitrary extreme XYZ.
